chunks.heading: CROP WEATHER WATCH
chunks.text: Summary Points of the CWWG meeting: I. Preliminary Report of area coverage under Rabi season Rabi crops: - As on January 03, 2025, the area sown under Rabi crops is 622.76 lakh ha as compared to 621.52 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. Of this, area of 319.74 lakh ha has been sown under wheat this year against the previous year area of 314.25 lakh ha (increase of 5.49 lakh ha). Rabi Horticulture Crops : - For Onion, Potato and Tomato, an area sown has been reported by the major producing States, 7.02 lakh ha, 17.14 lakh ha, 1.65 lakh ha as against total sown area of 5.78 lakh ha, 11.80 lakh ha, 1.30 lakh ha, respectively in the last year. II. Weather: - Light to moderate scattered/fairly widespread rainfall/snowfall likely over Western Himalayan Region and isolated to scattered rainfall over adjoining plains of northwest India during 1st half of the week. - Isolated to scattered rainfall likely over South Peninsular & adjoining central India during some days of the week. - Dense fog conditions during late night to early morning hours likely to continue over parts of North India till 09th January. - No significant change in minimum temperatures likely over northwest, Central & West India during next 3-4 days.

chunks.heading: CROP WEATHER WATCH
chunks.text:
- There is a low to moderate probability of cold wave conditions at isolated places over Punjab, Haryana, adjoining north Rajasthan & Himachal Pradesh during some days of the week. - Overall, rainfall is likely to be above normal over most parts of Central & South Peninsular India; normal to above normal over many parts of plains of northwest India; below normal over rest parts of the country during the week. III. Rainfall distribution:
- All India seasonal cumulative (01st Jan – 6th Jan 2025) rainfall in % departure from its Long Period Average (LPA) was (-)76%, with East & North East-India (-)99%, North- West India (-)59%, Central India (-)100% and South Peninsula (-)76%. IV. Water Reservoir Status: - As on 02nd January, 2025, the total live water storage in 155 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 132.293 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 73% of total live storage capacity (180.85 BCM). - The current year's storage is nearly 125 percent of last year's storage and 119 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. - The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period. V.

chunks.heading: CROP WEATHER WATCH
chunks.text: Groundwater Levels Scenario - About 66.6% of the total monitoring wells show depth to water level in the range of 0 to 5 m below ground level and 29.1% show depth to water level in the range of 5 to 10 m below ground level. As per decadal water level fluctuation with a mean (August 2014 to 2023) and August 2024 analysis, 64.9% of monitoring wells (8199) show a rise whereas 35.1% (4435) show a fall in August month. VI. Seeds: - For Rabi 2024-25, availability of certified/ quality seed in the country is 337.98 lakh quintals against the requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals indicating an overall surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals of seeds. VII. Fertilizers: - Fertilizers position is stated to be comfortable in all products. VIII. Pests & Diseases: - Intensity of pests and diseases, at some fields, has been reported to be above Economic Threshold Level for Maize (FAW) in Tamil Nadu. The advisory has been issued through NPSS and regular monitoring is being carried out. The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below Economic Threshold Level. Details of each sector have been enclosed at Annex.

chunks.heading: CROP WEATHER WATCH
chunks.text: Annex WEATHER OUTLOOK 01st Jan to 05th Jan, 2025: - During the week (26 Dec 2024 – 01-01-2025), excess rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 120%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01 Jan to 05 Jan 2025) is lower than LPA by 94%. Rainfall Forecast: 2nd Jan – 08th Jan 2025 - Light to moderate rainfall at many places likely over Northeastern states on 07th & 08th January. - A fresh Western Disturbance is likely to affect Northwest India from 10-12th January. Under its influence, Light to moderate rainfall/snowfall likely over Western Himalayan region and light rainfall over the plains of Northwest India during the same period. 09th Jan – 15th Jan 2025 - Under the influences of active western disturbance, light to moderate scattered/fairly widespread rainfall/snowfall likely over Western Himalayan Region and isolated to scattered rainfall over adjoining plains of northwest India during 1st half of the week. - Under the influence of likely formation of cyclonic circulation/ Low Pressure area, isolated to scattered rainfall likely over South Peninsular & adjoining central India during some days of the week.

chunks.heading: CROP WEATHER WATCH
chunks.text: - Overall, rainfall is likely to be above normal over most parts of Central & South Peninsular India; normal to above normal over many parts of plains of northwest India; below normal over rest parts of the country during the week. Temperature Forecast: 2nd Jan – 08th Jan 2025 - Minimum temperatures are expected to gradually rise by 2-3°C over Northwest India during the next five days. Over Central and East India, no significant change is expected for the next three days, followed by a gradual increase of 2- 3°C. In the Maharashtra region, a fall of 2-3°C is likely over the next two days, with no significant change thereafter. Gujarat is expected to experience no significant change in minimum temperatures over the next five days. - Dense fog conditions to prevail during night/early morning hours in some parts of Punjab & Haryana Chandigarh during 06th-08th; in isolated pockets of Punjab & Haryana, Chandigarh on 09th; Uttar Pradesh & Rajasthan during 06th - 08th, West Bengal & Sikkim, Jharkhand on 06th; Bihar on 06th; Assam & Meghalaya & Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram & Tripura on 06th January.

chunks.heading: CROP WEATHER WATCH
chunks.text: 09th Jan – 15th Jan 2025 - Minimum temperatures are likely to be between 4-8°C over many parts of north India (excluding Western Himalayan Region) and above 8°C over rest parts of the country during the week. - Minimum temperatures are likely to be near normal or slightly above normal over most parts of northwest & adjoining central India and northeast India. It is likely to below normal by 1-3°C over Peninsular & adjoining east India during the week. - There is a low to moderate probability of cold wave conditions at isolated places over Punjab, Haryana, adjoining north Rajasthan & Himachal Pradesh during some days of the week. - Dense fog is likely to occur in isolated places of Indo Gangetic plains during some days of the week. For more details login to IMD website. RESERVOIR STORAGE (as on 02nd January, 2025) - Current live storage in 155 reservoirs was 135.404 BCM (75%) of total live capacity of 180.85 BCM. - 143 reservoirs having storage more than 80% of normal storage. - 09 reservoirs having storage 51% to 80%. - 02 reservoirs having storage 31% to 50%. - 01 reservoir having storage up to 30 %.

chunks.text:
DAP: Di ammonium phosphate, MOP: Muriate of Potash, NPK: Complex fertilizer & SSP: Single Super Phosphate, Source: Fertilizer Division (DA&FW)/ Department of Fertilizer
PEST & DISEASE - Overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below Economic Threshold Level (ETL) except: RABI HORTICULTURE (As on 26th December, 2024) Onion: 7.02 lakh ha area has been sown in 2024-25 as compared to all India total area sown of 5.78 lakh ha in 2023-24. Potato: 17.14 lakh ha area has been sown in 2024-25 as compared to all India total area sown of 11.80 lakh ha in 2023-24. Tomato: 1.65 lakh ha area has been sown in 2024-25 as compared to all India total area sown of 1.30 lakh ha in 2023-24. PRICES - Mandi prices of Wheat (0.52%), Tur (1.09%), Gram (2.38%), Masur (2.51%), Moong (2.19%), Urad (8.20%), Mustard (0.94%), Soybean (2.49%) and Sunflower (14.99%) have increased week-on-week and prices of Rice (3.97%), Groundnut (0.16%) and Sesamum (3.30%) have decreased week-on-week. All India retail prices of Rice (0.50%), Gram (0.11%), Masur (0.21%), Moong (0.24%) and Urad (0.12%) increased week-on-week and prices of Wheat (0.18%), Tur (0.52%), Mustard (0.43%) and Soya bean (1.15%) and have decreased week-on-week.
